$comment: DriveOne Direct OWNER series: customers who paid for a DOD vehicle service contract. Runs the length of the Budco loan (LOAN_MONTHS, usually 30). Voice: Red Bull register, deadpan, confident, useful. No exclamation points. No em dashes or en dashes. Never call it a warranty. Every email carries the claims line and the roadside line in a fixed strip under the header. One job per email. Diminished Value Protection is a ONE YEAR term: say so, and warn before it lapses. Openbay+ sends its own login email; we point to it, we do not invent login steps. Referral link is driveonedirect.com/?ref=<contract_number>. Optional `video` block renders a thumbnail card after the P.S.

campaign.name: DriveOne Direct: Owner series
campaign.audience: driveonedirect.com customers with a paid, Budco confirmed contract

variables.DV_END_DATE: one year from your start date

campaign.variablesNote: FIRST_NAME and RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL are Resend built-ins. REVIEW_URL is the Google Business Profile short link, to be supplied by Ryan. REFERRAL_URL = https://www.driveonedirect.com/?ref=<contract_number>&utm_source=email&utm_medium=owner_series&utm_campaign=referral. PLATE_URL = https://www.driveonedirect.com/?utm_source=email&utm_medium=owner_series&utm_campaign=second_car#quote. Fallbacks never look numeric.

emails.goal: Put the two numbers in their phone. Set expectations for the series.
emails.subject: Two numbers to save before you forget this email
emails.subjectAlt: {{{FIRST_NAME}}}, your {{{VEHICLE}}} is covered. Here is the part to keep.
emails.preheader: Claims and roadside. Save both now, use them never, hopefully.
emails.headline:
Save two numbers.
Then go live your life.
body: Your {{{VEHICLE}}} is covered as of {{{START_DATE}}}. The contract is {{{CONTRACT}}}. You will not need to remember that number, because it is at the top and bottom of every email we send you.

The two numbers you do want in your phone are the ones under the logo above. Claims, which the shop calls before touching anything. Roadside, which you call from a shoulder at 11pm. Save them now while this is open and you will never search for them while stressed.
emails.after: Over the length of your plan we will send one short note at a time: how to use Openbay+ to pay less for service, what Diminished Value Protection actually does, and the one thing to check on your payment plan so it never lapses. No fluff. Unsubscribe on every one.
emails.ctaNote: Tapping it on a phone opens the dialer so you can save it as a contact. Call it only when something breaks.
emails.ps: If you were expecting a confetti cannon: budget cuts. The coverage is the confetti.

emails.goal: Openbay+ account exists. Tell them where the login email is and what the membership does.
emails.subject: You own an Openbay+ membership. It emailed you.
emails.subjectAlt: The part of your plan that saves money before anything breaks
emails.preheader: Openbay+ came with your plan. Find its email, set a password, book cheaper service.
emails.headline:
Your plan pays for
repairs. Openbay+ makes
the maintenance cheaper.
body: When your payment cleared, an Openbay+ membership was opened in your name, on the same email address this landed in. Openbay sent you a separate email to activate it. Search your inbox for Openbay. If it went to promotions or spam, that is where it is hiding.

Openbay is a booking service for ASE-certified shops. You pick a shop, pick a time, see the price up front, and the member discount comes off at the shop. No haggling at the counter, no mystery line items.

card.title: WHAT OPENBAY+ DOES
rows: Member pricing on service and repairs
Use any ASE shop; Openbay just makes finding one easy

emails.after: You do not have to use Openbay for covered claims. You can take the {{{VEHICLE}}} anywhere ASE-certified. Openbay is for the stuff the plan does not pay for: oil, brakes, tires, the quiet money.
emails.ctaNote: Log in with the email on your contract. If you never got the activation email, reply to this one and we will resend it.
emails.ps: Yes, you can book an oil change at 11pm from the couch. We checked. It felt great.

emails.goal: Explain Diminished Value Protection, the contract number, the one year term, how to use it.
emails.subject: The benefit on your contract nobody explains
emails.subjectAlt: What VASDVP on your welcome email means
emails.preheader: Diminished Value Protection, up to $5,000, included for one year. Here is what it is.
emails.headline:
Somebody taps your
bumper. Your car is
worth less forever.
body: Here is a thing that happens. Someone rear ends you at a light. Their insurance fixes the bumper. The car looks perfect. And it is now worth thousands less, because it has an accident on its history and buyers can read.

That gap is called diminished value. Your plan includes protection for it, up to $5,000, for one year from your start date. Its own contract number is {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}. It is on your welcome email too.

card.title: IF IT HAPPENS
rows: Photos of the damage and the other plate, on the spot
Get the police or insurance report number
Ascent walks you through the claim

hero.label: PROTECTED UNTIL
hero.sub: up to $5,000 in diminished value, one year term
hero.fine: We will remind you before it ends. This is not something to think about until you need it.

emails.after: Most people have never heard of diminished value until they try to sell a car with a repaired fender and get an offer that makes no sense. You now know. That is the whole email.
emails.ctaNote: Same Ascent number as claims. Say Diminished Value and give them {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}.
emails.ps: The photo of the other plate is the step people skip. We cannot cover forgetting it.

emails.goal: Review ask while it is fresh. Google Business Profile link.
emails.subject: Was that easy? Tell someone who is not us.
emails.subjectAlt: Two weeks in. One favor, thirty seconds.
emails.preheader: If buying this was easier than you expected, a review helps the next person skip the dealership desk.
emails.headline:
You bought this without
talking to anyone.
Tell people that.
body: Two weeks ago you bought a vehicle service contract on a phone, in minutes, without a finance manager sliding a menu across a desk. Most people do not know that is possible. They think the desk is the only door.
A review is how they find out. Thirty seconds, no essay required. Say what it was like to buy, not what you think of the coverage, because you have not needed it yet and we hope you never do.
emails.after: If it was not easy, reply to this email instead and tell us what went wrong. We read every one and we would rather fix it than collect it.
emails.ctaNote: Opens Google. One star rating and one sentence is plenty.
emails.ps: Every review that mentions the word dealership makes someone here smile in a way that is hard to describe.

emails.goal: The claims playbook. Shop calls before work. Direct pay. $100.
emails.subject: How a claim actually goes, so you never guess
emails.subjectAlt: The three sentence version of your contract
emails.preheader: Shop calls Ascent first. Ascent pays the shop. You pay $100. That is the process.
emails.headline:
The shop calls us.
Not you. That is
the whole trick.
body: The single thing that makes a claim go wrong is a shop that starts work before calling. Then it is a reimbursement argument instead of a covered repair. So the rule is simple and worth saying out loud once.
Any ASE-certified shop. Before they touch anything, they call Ascent at 866-660-7003 with contract {{{CONTRACT}}}. Ascent authorizes. Ascent pays the shop directly. You pay $100 and drive home.

card.title: HOW A CLAIM GOES
rows: Take the {{{VEHICLE}}} to any ASE-certified shop
Shop calls Ascent at 866-660-7003 before work starts
Ascent authorizes and pays the shop

emails.after: If a shop says they do not work with service contracts, that is a shop choice, not a coverage problem. Openbay+ will find you one that does, usually closer than you think.
emails.cta: Find an ASE shop on Openbay →
emails.ctaNote: Good to know before you need it. Terrible to learn on a flatbed.
emails.ps: Rental reimbursement up to $250 per claim and trip interruption up to $450 are in there too. Ask Ascent on the call.

emails.goal: Budco payment plan: autopay card, what happens if it fails, the number to update it.
emails.subject: The one boring thing that keeps your coverage alive
emails.subjectAlt: Month one. Check the card.
emails.preheader: Your plan is paid monthly to Budco. If the card changes, the coverage can lapse. One number fixes it.
emails.headline:
Coverage runs on a
card. Cards expire.
That is the risk.
body: Your {{{MONTHLY}}} a month goes to Budco Financial Services, who run the 0% plan. Budco is not us and not Ascent. They are the payment company, and they are good at exactly one thing.

The only way most people lose coverage is a card that expired, got replaced after fraud, or hit a limit. The payment fails, nobody notices, and the plan lapses right before the transmission does. Keep Budco's number and update them the day your card changes.

card.title: PAYMENT PLAN
rows: Same number. They do not sell anything.

emails.after: If a payment ever fails you will hear from Budco first. Call them back. A missed payment is a phone call; a lapsed plan is a repair bill.
emails.ctaNote: Payment questions only. Coverage questions still go to Ascent.
emails.ps: This is the least interesting email in the series. It is also the one that matters most. Life is like that.

emails.goal: First actual Openbay booking. Oil change interval based on mileage at purchase.
emails.subject: Your first cheaper oil change
emails.subjectAlt: Book it on Openbay. Pay less. Keep the receipt.
emails.preheader: Routine service through Openbay+ costs less and keeps your coverage records clean.
emails.headline:
Oil changes are not
covered. Overpaying
for them is optional.
body: Your plan covers the expensive surprises, not the scheduled stuff. The scheduled stuff is where Openbay+ earns its keep: book an ASE-certified shop, see the price up front, member discount off at the counter.

You were at {{{MILEAGE}}} when you bought the plan. If you are close to an oil change, book it now and keep the receipt. Service records are what a claims adjuster asks for first, and a folder of Openbay receipts answers the question before it is asked.

card.title: THE HABIT
rows: Every receipt, in one folder or one email label
The {{{VEHICLE}}} lasts longer. Shocking, we know.

emails.after: Keeping records is the least glamorous advice in car ownership and the most useful. A plan pays for covered failures on a maintained car. Openbay makes the maintained part cheap and the records part automatic.
emails.ctaNote: Log in with the email on your contract.
emails.ps: Forward the Openbay receipt to yourself with the subject {{{VEHICLE}}}. Future you will find it in two seconds.

emails.goal: Referral: $100 gift card when a friend buys through their link.
emails.subject: $100 if a friend buys one of these
emails.subjectAlt: Your referral link, and what it pays
emails.preheader: Send your link. If they buy a plan, you get a $100 gift card. They get the same deal you got.
emails.headline:
You know someone with
a car and a bad feeling
about the transmission.
body: Everyone does. The friend with the 90,000 mile SUV who changes the subject when it makes a noise. Send them your link. If they buy a plan, we send you a $100 gift card after their plan is active for 30 days.
They get exactly what you got: a quote in minutes, a plan priced without a desk markup, 0% financing, any ASE shop. You get to be the person who told them before the noise turned into a bill.

card.title: HOW IT WORKS
rows: Send your link, text or email
They buy a plan through it
30 days later, $100 gift card to you
No limit. Know a lot of people.

emails.after: No forms, no codes to remember. The link carries your contract number so we know it was you.
emails.ctaNote: Your link: {{{REFERRAL_URL}}}
emails.ps: The gift card is real. The 30 day wait is because we have met the internet.

emails.goal: Second vehicle: plate scan, free quote, add a plan to the household.
emails.subject: The other car in the driveway
emails.subjectAlt: Scan a plate, get a price, cover the second one
emails.preheader: Point your phone at a plate. Get a quote for the other car in about a minute.
emails.headline:
You covered one car.
The other one is
watching, uncovered.
body: Three months in and the {{{VEHICLE}}} is handled. Most driveways have a second car, and it is usually the older one, which is the one that breaks.

The quote tool reads a license plate from your phone camera, decodes the vehicle, and prices a plan. Same deal: $100 deductible, 0% plan, any ASE shop, Openbay+ and Diminished Value Protection included. About a minute, no call.

card.title: SCAN A PLATE
rows: Open the link on your phone
Point the camera at any plate in your driveway
See the price. Buy it or close the tab.
Spouse, kid, the truck you keep for reasons

emails.after: A second plan does not change the first. Separate contract, separate payment, same two phone numbers you already saved.
emails.ctaNote: Works on any car in the household. The plate does not have to be yours; the car does.
emails.ps: If your second car is a 2004 something with a cassette deck, we respect that, and it may not rate. The tool will tell you.

emails.goal: DV refresher framed as a how-to after an accident.
emails.subject: If someone hits you this month, read this first
emails.subjectAlt: The checklist for a minor accident
emails.preheader: Five things to do at the scene. Diminished Value Protection is why the fifth one matters.
emails.headline:
After a fender bender,
the first ten minutes
decide the next $5,000.
body: Nobody plans for the parking lot tap. But the money you keep or lose is decided right there, before the tow, before the body shop, before anybody is calm.

Your Diminished Value Protection, contract {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}, covers up to $5,000 of the value your {{{VEHICLE}}} loses from having an accident on record. It is active until {{{DV_END_DATE}}}. It works best when you have the paperwork.

card.title: AT THE SCENE
rows: Photos: both cars, both plates, the intersection
Police report or insurance claim number
Body shop estimate, even if their insurer pays

emails.after: Their insurance pays to fix the car. Your DV protection addresses what the fix does not: the resale hit. Two different checks for two different losses.
emails.ctaNote: Contract {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}. One year term, ends {{{DV_END_DATE}}}.
emails.ps: Screenshot the card above. It is the only part of this email you need at the scene.

emails.goal: Openbay for wear items. Price transparency.
emails.subject: Brakes and tires are not covered. Here is the cheaper way.
emails.subjectAlt: The wear items, priced before you arrive
emails.preheader: Openbay+ shows the price before you book. That is the whole difference.
emails.headline:
The parts that wear out
are the parts shops
pad the bill on.
body: Brakes, tires, wipers, batteries. Nobody covers them, because they are supposed to wear out. They are also where a walk-in customer pays the most, because the price is decided after the car is on the lift.

Openbay+ flips the order. You see the shop's price for the job before you book, the member discount is applied, and the appointment is set. If a shop adds something at the counter, you knew the baseline.
emails.after: Five months in, the {{{VEHICLE}}} is probably due for something. Book it where the price is written down.
emails.ctaNote: Log in with the email on your contract.
emails.ps: A shop that will not quote before the lift is telling you how the bill gets made.

emails.goal: Six month check: card on file, a short recap, the numbers again.
emails.subject: Six months. One thing to check.
emails.subjectAlt: Halfway to a year. Is the card still good?
emails.preheader: Six months in. Confirm the payment card, keep the two numbers, carry on.
emails.headline:
Half a year covered.
Thirty seconds of
admin to keep it.
body: Six months ago you covered the {{{VEHICLE}}}. Since then the plan has sat there doing the job coverage does best, which is nothing, loudly.

Cards expire on a schedule you did not choose. If yours has changed since {{{START_DATE}}}, Budco needs the new one, or the {{{MONTHLY}}} payment fails and the plan goes with it. One call. Then forget about it for another six.
emails.after: That is the list. Nothing to buy, nothing to renew. The plan keeps running as long as the payments do.
emails.ctaNote: Only if it changed. Otherwise close this and enjoy your day.
emails.ps: Six months without a claim is the goal, not a waste. You bought the plan so the bad day would be boring.

emails.goal: Seasonal readiness via Openbay: battery, tires, wipers, coolant. Roadside number.
emails.subject: The season that kills batteries is coming
emails.subjectAlt: A pre-season check, booked where the price is posted
emails.preheader: Batteries, tires, wipers. Check them before the weather does.
emails.headline:
Weather does not
break cars. It finds
the ones already weak.
body: Every season has a part it picks on. Cold kills batteries. Heat kills them too, slower. Rain finds the wipers you meant to replace. None of that is a covered failure, all of it is a Tuesday ruined.
A pre-season check through Openbay+ is cheap and the price is posted before you book. If something is marginal, you fix it on your schedule instead of the weather's.

card.title: PRE-SEASON LIST
rows: Load test, especially past year three
If they streak, they are done
877-626-0880, in case the list was late

emails.after: If the list is late and the {{{VEHICLE}}} does not start, roadside is included: up to three events a year, any hour. That number is under the logo on every email we send.
emails.ctaNote: Openbay+, member pricing, ASE-certified shop of your choosing.
emails.ps: A jump start at 6am in a parking garage is a roadside event. It is also a sign. Book the battery test.

emails.goal: Second referral ask with a different angle: the person who just bought a used car.
emails.subject: Know anyone who just bought a used car?
emails.subjectAlt: The thirty day window after a used car purchase
emails.preheader: The best time to cover a used car is right after buying it. Your link, their $100 savings for you.
emails.headline:
Someone you know just
bought a used car and
said no to the desk.
body: Good. The desk markup was real. But they walked out with no coverage and a car that has already had one owner, and the first big repair is usually inside the first two years.
Send your link. They get a quote in a minute with no desk and no markup. If they buy, we send you a $100 gift card after their plan is active for 30 days. Same as last time, no limit.

hero.label: YOUR REFERRAL LINK
hero.sub: per friend whose plan activates through your link

emails.after: Facebook Marketplace, a private sale, a cousin: anyone who bought without a finance office is exactly who this was built for.
emails.ctaNote: Text it, email it, put it in the group chat.
emails.ps: The group chat move works more often than you would think.

emails.goal: Roadside, rental, trip interruption. Put the roadside number in the phone, again.
emails.subject: The bad day kit, nine months in
emails.subjectAlt: Roadside, rental, hotel. What the plan does on the shoulder.
emails.preheader: Three events a year of roadside. Rental up to $250 per claim. Trip interruption up to $450.
emails.headline:
The car dying is the
cheap part. The rest of
the day is the bill.
body: A breakdown is not one problem. It is a tow, then a rental, then two days of asking people for rides, then possibly a hotel because it happened three hundred miles from your bed.

Your plan handles that part too. Roadside is included, up to three events a year. Rental reimbursement up to $250 per covered claim. Trip interruption up to $450 if you are far from home. The claims call to Ascent is what turns all three on.

card.title: ON A BAD DAY
rows: 877-626-0880, any hour, up to 3 events a year
Ask Ascent on that call. Keep receipts.

emails.after: None of this needs a good attitude on the day. It needs the two numbers, which you saved nine months ago. If you did not, there is no judgment, and they are under the logo.
emails.ctaNote: Goes in your phone under R. Thank a past version of yourself later.
emails.ps: Trip interruption only counts if you are a real distance from home. A breakdown in your own driveway is just a Tuesday.

emails.goal: Diminished Value Protection lapses at 12 months. Warn at month 10 and tell them what to do.
emails.subject: Your Diminished Value Protection ends in two months
emails.subjectAlt: A date to know: {{{DV_END_DATE}}}
emails.preheader: Up to $5,000 of diminished value protection, included for year one. It ends {{{DV_END_DATE}}}.
emails.headline:
Year one of Diminished
Value Protection ends
{{{DV_END_DATE}}}.
body: When you bought the plan, Diminished Value Protection came with it for one year, up to $5,000. Contract {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}. That year ends on {{{DV_END_DATE}}}.

Two things to know. One: if you have had an accident on record since {{{START_DATE}}} and have not filed, call Ascent now, not after the date. Two: your vehicle service contract on the {{{VEHICLE}}} keeps running for the full {{{COVERAGE_MONTHS}}}. Only the DV piece has a one year term.

card.title: WHAT CHANGES AND WHAT DOES NOT

emails.after: If you want to keep Diminished Value Protection past year one, reply to this email and we will tell you what is available. We are not going to pretend it renews itself.
emails.cta: Had an accident this year? Call Ascent →
emails.ctaNote: Contract {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}. Before {{{DV_END_DATE}}}.
emails.ps: Most people will never use this. The ones who do are glad someone wrote it down.

emails.goal: Second car, framed around family members (kid driver, parent).
emails.subject: The teenager has a car now. So does the risk.
emails.subjectAlt: Cover the car that worries you most
emails.preheader: The car that scares you is the one to quote. Scan the plate, see the number.
emails.headline:
Every family has one
car that worries
everyone else.
body: The kid's first car. The parent's old sedan. The one that gets driven hard and serviced never. Almost a year in with the {{{VEHICLE}}}, you know what a plan feels like: the noise is just a noise, not a bill.

Point your phone at that car's plate. The tool prices a plan in about a minute. If it rates, you can put it on a 0% plan like yours and give the person who drives it the same two phone numbers you have.

card.title: WORTH QUOTING
rows: Driven by someone learning what a car costs
Past 80,000 miles and still daily driven
Sits a lot, which is how batteries and seals die

emails.after: Separate contract, separate payment, same shop network, same claims line. The person driving it never has to learn how a claim works. They hand the shop the number.
emails.ctaNote: About a minute. No call. Close the tab if the price is not right.
emails.ps: Teaching a new driver to say have the shop call this number first is the most useful thing in this email.

emails.goal: Anniversary. Recap. Card check. DV lapsed. Review ask again, softly.
emails.subject: One year covered. Here is the recap.
emails.subjectAlt: Happy anniversary to your {{{VEHICLE}}}
emails.preheader: A year in. What the plan did, what to check, what changed.
emails.headline:
A year ago you skipped
the desk. Here is what
that bought.
body: Twelve months of a plan on the {{{VEHICLE}}}: a fixed $100 deductible on covered repairs, roadside on call, a rental if a claim needed one, Openbay+ for everything else, and a year of Diminished Value Protection that ended this week.
The mechanical coverage keeps going. {{{COVERAGE_MONTHS}}} total, which means the plan outlasts the payments. Two things to do today, and then nothing for another year.

card.title: YEAR ONE CHECK
rows: Year one ended. Reply if you want options.
If year one was fine, say so below

emails.after: If the only thing this plan did all year was sit there, that was the point. You bought boring. Boring is what it looks like when it works.
emails.ctaNote: Skip it if you already did. We will not ask twice in the same year.
emails.ps: We would send a cake. Email cannot carry cake. We checked.

emails.goal: What to do when the car makes a new noise: do not wait, call, covered diagnostics via claim.
emails.subject: That new noise. Do not wait it out.
emails.subjectAlt: Noises get more expensive with time
emails.preheader: A new noise is a free phone call away from an answer. Waiting turns it into a bill.
emails.headline:
Every expensive repair
was a cheap noise
three weeks earlier.
body: Fourteen months in, the {{{VEHICLE}}} will eventually make a sound it did not make before. The instinct is to turn the radio up. The instinct is wrong, and with a plan, it is also unnecessary.

Take it to an ASE-certified shop, book it through Openbay+ if you want the price posted first, and have the shop call Ascent before they do anything. If the cause is a covered failure, the repair is covered. If it is not, you paid for a diagnosis instead of a tow.

card.title: WHEN IT MAKES A NOISE
rows: Note when it happens: cold, turning, braking, speed
Covered failure: $100. Not covered: you still caught it early.

emails.after: The plan pays for covered parts that fail. It does not pay for the extra damage caused by driving on a failed part for a month. Early is cheaper in every version of this story.
emails.ctaNote: Tell the shop there is a service contract before they start.
emails.ps: The radio trick has never once fixed a wheel bearing. We have looked into it.

emails.goal: Third referral ask: the coworker angle, quick.
emails.subject: The coworker with the check engine light
emails.subjectAlt: $100 for you if they finally deal with it
emails.preheader: Everyone has one. Your link gets them a quote in a minute and you a $100 gift card.
emails.headline:
The light has been on
since spring. You both
know it.
body: Sixteen months in, you are the person at work who has a plan and does not flinch at shop estimates. Someone there has a check engine light they have been ignoring since the weather was different.
Send them your link. A quote in a minute, no desk, 0% plan. If they buy, you get a $100 gift card once their plan is active for 30 days. It is the same link as always, and it still works.

hero.label: YOUR LINK
hero.sub: per friend whose plan activates through it

emails.after: A check engine light is not always a covered failure, and a plan is not a reason to keep ignoring one. But a plan is the reason the diagnosis is not scary.
emails.ctaNote: Text works best. People open texts from people they know.
emails.ps: If the coworker is your boss, this is also a performance review strategy. Not a good one, but a strategy.

emails.goal: 18 month card check and a reminder the loan ends before coverage does.
emails.subject: Eighteen months. Twelve payments left.
emails.subjectAlt: The card check, and what happens when the payments stop
emails.preheader: A year and a half in. Confirm the card. Then a note about the end of the payment plan.
emails.headline:
The payments end
before the coverage
does. On purpose.
body: Eighteen months in on the {{{VEHICLE}}}. Your Budco plan runs {{{LOAN_MONTHS}}}, so you are past the halfway mark on payments. The coverage runs {{{COVERAGE_MONTHS}}}. When the last payment clears, the plan keeps going. Nothing to renew, nothing to re-sign.
The one thing between you and that is the card on file. If it changed, Budco needs the new one. If it did not, this email is already over.
emails.after: A lapsed card at month eighteen costs you the plan you are mostly done paying for. That would be a bad trade. Check the card.
emails.ctaNote: Budco, payments only.
emails.ps: Yes, this is the same email as month six with the numbers changed. The card does not care that you have heard it before.

emails.goal: Coverage transfers to a buyer. Makes the car easier to sell. Call Ascent.
emails.subject: Selling the car? The plan goes with it.
emails.subjectAlt: A car with a service contract sells faster
emails.preheader: Coverage transfers to the buyer. That is a selling point, not a loose end.
emails.headline:
A used car with a plan
is a different listing
than one without.
body: Twenty months is when a lot of people start thinking about the next car. If the {{{VEHICLE}}} is headed to a listing, know this: the plan can transfer to the buyer. Remaining coverage, same terms, same claims line.

A buyer looking at two similar cars picks the one that comes with a service contract. You can say so in the listing. Call Ascent before the sale to handle the transfer paperwork, and settle the Budco balance so it transfers clean.

card.title: TO TRANSFER
rows: Give the buyer the contract number and the two phone numbers
Put it in the listing. It is a feature.

emails.after: If you are not selling, file this under good to know. If you are, it is worth real money in the listing and real calm for whoever buys it.
emails.ctaNote: Transfer rules and any fee vary by state. Ascent will tell you exactly.
emails.ps: A listing that says comes with a transferable service contract gets fewer tire kickers. That is a technical term.

emails.goal: Major mileage service interval via Openbay. Records matter for the back half of the term.
emails.subject: The big service interval, priced before you go
emails.subjectAlt: Timing belt, fluids, plugs: book it where the price is posted
emails.preheader: The expensive scheduled service is cheaper with a posted price and a member discount.
emails.headline:
Every car has one
expensive service.
Book it with the price up front.
body: Somewhere between 60,000 and 100,000 miles, every car has the service interval that makes people wince: belts, fluids, plugs, sometimes a water pump while they are in there. It is not a covered failure. It is maintenance, and it is the one that shops love to quote after the car is on the lift.

Book it through Openbay+ and the price is posted first, with the member discount applied. Keep the receipt. The back half of your coverage term is when a claims adjuster is most likely to ask for maintenance records, and this is the record they ask about.
emails.after: Doing the big service on time is also how the {{{VEHICLE}}} gets to the end of the coverage term without the big failure. Boring, again, is the goal.
emails.ctaNote: Openbay+ member pricing.
emails.ps: If a shop quotes it without seeing the car, that is a feature of Openbay, not a red flag. Posted pricing is the point.

emails.goal: Two year recap, card check, referral line, review line. Short.
emails.subject: Two years covered. Short recap.
emails.subjectAlt: Year two of the {{{VEHICLE}}}, in one card
emails.preheader: Two years in. The card, the numbers, and six payments to go.
emails.headline:
Two years, one plan,
zero finance offices.
body: Two years ago you bought a plan for the {{{VEHICLE}}} on your phone. Since then: a $100 deductible on anything covered, roadside on call, Openbay+ for the rest, and a stack of emails that were, we hope, shorter than most.
Six payments left on the Budco plan, give or take. Coverage continues past that. The two phone numbers are the same. The card check is the same. Thirty seconds and you are done for the year.
emails.after: If someone you know bought a car this year, the referral link at the bottom still pays $100. If year two was uneventful, a review saying so is the most honest kind.
emails.ctaNote: Or skip it. Two years without needing us is its own review.
emails.ps: Still no cake. Still checked.

emails.goal: Final stretch of payments. Do not let the card lapse at the end. What happens after.
emails.subject: Three payments left. Do not trip at the finish.
emails.subjectAlt: The end of the payment plan, and what happens next
emails.preheader: Almost paid off. The card has to survive three more months. Then the plan runs on its own.
emails.headline:
Three payments left.
The plan outlives
all of them.
body: You are at the end of the Budco plan on the {{{VEHICLE}}}. Three payments, roughly, and then nothing more to pay. The coverage does not stop; it runs to the end of the {{{COVERAGE_MONTHS}}} term.

The only way to lose it this close to the end is a card that fails in the last stretch. Confirm it is good through the final payment. Budco will send a payoff confirmation when it clears. Keep it with your welcome email.
emails.after: After the payoff, these emails slow down. The numbers stay the same. The plan stays the same. You just stop hearing from Budco, which is the best thing anyone can say about a lender.
emails.ctaNote: 888-352-7901. Three minutes, once.
emails.ps: Tripping at the finish line is a real thing in car plans. It is almost always a card.

emails.goal: Loan paid off. Coverage continues. Final thanks, referral, review, second car. Series ends.
emails.subject: Paid off. Covered until {{{COVERAGE_MONTHS}}} is up.
emails.subjectAlt: The last payment cleared. Here is what that means.
emails.preheader: The Budco plan is done. The coverage is not. One last note from us.
emails.headline:
The payments are done.
The coverage is not.
This is the last one.
body: Your Budco plan on the {{{VEHICLE}}} is paid. Nothing else is owed. The vehicle service contract, {{{CONTRACT}}}, keeps running until the end of its {{{COVERAGE_MONTHS}}} term, with the same $100 deductible, the same roadside, the same Openbay+ access.

This is the last scheduled email in the series. The two numbers stay in your phone. If something breaks, the shop calls Ascent. If you sell, the plan transfers. If you buy another car, the plate tool is still there.
emails.after: Thank you for buying this the way it was meant to be bought: on your own terms, in a few minutes, without anyone across a desk. If you tell one person that was possible, you have done more for us than any ad.
emails.ctaNote: Your link still pays $100 for every friend whose plan activates.
emails.ps: We said we would stop at the end of the plan. This is us stopping. The numbers do not expire.

sms.$comment: Sendblue, iMessage/SMS. Only to contacts with recorded SMS consent; honor STOP. Under 300 characters. Brand name, no links in the first text (deliverability), links after. Numbers written out. Each carries a STOP line on first contact.

messages.text: DriveOne Direct: {{{FIRST_NAME}}}, your {{{VEHICLE}}} is covered. Save these two: Claims 866-660-7003 (the shop calls this before work). Roadside 877-626-0880 (24/7). That is the whole system. Reply STOP to opt out.

DriveOne Direct: Openbay+ came with your plan and emailed you a login. Search your inbox for Openbay (check promotions). Book ASE shops with the price posted and the member discount on. {{{OPENBAY_URL}}}
DriveOne Direct: two weeks in. If buying this on your phone was easier than a dealership desk, a 30 second Google review helps the next person find the door: {{{REVIEW_URL}}}

DriveOne Direct: your {{{MONTHLY}}} goes to Budco, who run the 0% plan. If your card ever changes, call Budco at 888-352-7901 that day. A missed payment is a phone call. A lapsed plan is a repair bill.
DriveOne Direct: know someone with a car and a bad feeling about the transmission? Your link: {{{REFERRAL_URL}}} If they buy, you get a $100 gift card after 30 days. No limit.
DriveOne Direct: the other car in the driveway is watching, uncovered. Point your phone at its plate and get a price in about a minute: {{{PLATE_URL}}}
DriveOne Direct: six months covered. One check: is the payment card still valid? If it changed, Budco 888-352-7901. Claims 866-660-7003. Roadside 877-626-0880. Done for another six.

DriveOne Direct: your Diminished Value Protection (up to $5,000) ends {{{DV_END_DATE}}}. Had an accident on record this year and not filed? Call Ascent 866-660-7003 before that date, contract {{{DV_CONTRACT}}}. Mechanical coverage continues.

DriveOne Direct: one year covered on the {{{VEHICLE}}}. Card still good? 888-352-7901 if not. Year one DV protection has ended; reply if you want options. The plan keeps going. Thanks for skipping the desk.
DriveOne Direct: 18 months in, about 12 payments left. The payments end before the coverage does. Only a failed card can break that. Budco 888-352-7901 if yours changed.
DriveOne Direct: about three payments left on the {{{VEHICLE}}}. Keep the card good through the last one and the plan runs to the end of its term with nothing more owed. Budco 888-352-7901.

DriveOne Direct: paid off. Coverage on the {{{VEHICLE}}} continues to the end of its term. Claims 866-660-7003. Roadside 877-626-0880. Referral still pays $100: {{{REFERRAL_URL}}} This is our last scheduled text.
